newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries edge lower in Tokyo on dollar's fall.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries edge lower in Tokyo on dollar's fall.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries edged slightly lower by Tokyo midday on Tuesday in reaction to the dollar's fall from the previous New York close, traders said.
Despite the losses, market sentiment was turning stronger following the recent rallies, but activity was thin amid a lack of strong trading factors this morning, they said.
"Underlying sentiment is improving. We may see further price gains after the quarterly refunding," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 96-24/32, yielding 6.88 percent, against 96-26/32 in New York on Monday.
The Treasury will sell $17 billion worth of three-year notes on Tuesday and $12 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday.
"Besides the quarterly refunding, there is nothing much to focus on this week," another brokerage trader said.
The June T-bond futures contract rose 2/32 to 110-3/32 from the previous close.

"Japanese investors' interest in buying Treasuries is growing as credit-tightening fears are fading slightly in reaction to the outcome of recent U.S. economic data," the second trader said. "Actual purchases have not been spotted yet, but they may start buying after the refunding."
